summary: After Oblivion is an educational and interactive video game that rescues the history of 13 objects and spacecraft on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. Featuring a customizable avatar, narrations, mini-games, and bilingual support (Spanish/English), it brings science and space exploration to new generations in a fun way.
details:
After Oblivion is an educational and interactive video game that seeks to rescue the stories of objects, spacecraft, probes, and space mission vehicles that remain on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space.

The video game functions as a space exploration adventure. At the start, the player can create and customize their own astronaut and choose their name. Afterward, they explore different scenarios through an interactive map, where they discover 13 space objects and learn about their histories through first-person narrations and animated scenes. They can also answer questions about each mission and participate in five mini-games: driving a rover, landing a spacecraft, classifying objects according to their location, matching spacecraft with their names, and ordering events in a story. Upon completing activities, they earn stars and badges, while their progress is saved in the browser. Additionally, it features options in Spanish and English, voice narration, and links to consult NASA information.

Among its main benefits are facilitating learning about the history of space exploration, sparking interest in astronomy and technology, and strengthening skills such as memory, observation, attention, and logical thinking. By presenting scientific information through stories and interactive activities, we aim for children and youth to learn in an entertaining and participatory way.

The impact we hope to generate is bringing science and space exploration closer to new generations, promoting curiosity and interest in STEM fields. In the future, we want to improve the animations, incorporate new stories, and make the video game usable as a complementary educational resource in elementary and middle schools.

To develop the project, we used HTML to structure the content, CSS to design the interface, scenarios, and animations, and JavaScript to program the interactions, narrations, mini-games, and progress system. We also used Claude, an artificial intelligence tool that supported us during the development process, code generation and review, and problem-solving. The project was developed as a web application, so it did not require specialized hardware.

The creativity of our proposal lies in giving a voice, personality, and history to space objects that usually go unnoticed. Instead of presenting only scientific data, we transform their experiences into interactive tales narrated from their own perspective. Thus, each player can learn not only where these objects ended up, but also what they did and why their contributions remain important.

During development, we primarily considered our target audience, ease of use, accessibility, educational value, the veracity of the information, and the player experience. We also took into account the inclusion of two languages, voice narrations, pressure-free activities, and a reward system that motivates players to continue exploring.

With "After Oblivion," we want to convey that a mission does not lose its importance when it ends. Its discoveries remain, and its legacy can inspire those who will continue to explore the universe.

Every mission leaves an echo.
